title: Whitelisting an Agent Spell creates authority that expires, capped by a configurable maxDelay of about seven days
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.3.1.1.2.4 defines a configurable `maxDelay` setting "the maximum duration between the whitelisting of the Agent Spell in the Sky Core Spell and the execution of the Agent Spell," with a recommended value of seven days. The stated rationale: "this feature ensures Spells do not linger indefinitely, enforcing timely processing and reducing risks from delayed or forgotten actions."

This is the necessary complement to decoupling approval from execution. Once a Sky Core Spell only whitelists a codehash rather than executing it, an approved Spell becomes a standing option that someone may exercise later — and the world in which the vote was cast is not the world in which it might be executed. Market conditions, parameters and other approved changes all move.

`maxDelay` therefore encodes a claim about what a governance decision *is*: not a permanent grant but a mandate with a shelf life, valid under approximately the conditions in which it was approved. Beyond the window, re-authorization is required rather than assumed.

It also removes a class of ambush. Without expiry, an unexecuted whitelist entry is a latent action that can be triggered at a moment chosen by whoever is watching — including a moment specifically chosen to be harmful. Bounding the window bounds that optionality, and pairs with `drop()` for explicit revocation: one mechanism for when someone notices a problem, one for when nobody does.
description: Prevents approved Spells lingering indefinitely, so a stale mandate cannot execute into changed conditions; timely processing becomes a contract-enforced property rather than an operational habit.
